messages:
alex (partnerships): hey folks, inbound from OpenModelX — they want to onboard an open LLM to our model catalog and discuss licensing + distribution for Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployments. quick sync? :eyes:

maria (legal): do we have the model license text yet? commercial / redistribution permissions are the key. many "open" models still forbid certain commercial uses.

alex (partnerships): they sent a link to their repo and a short summary. license header says ‘OpenModelX License v1.0 (permissive)’, but no redistribution clause spelled out. asking if we can list on hosted API, offer as dedicated reserved pool, and include in Private deployments (customer-managed infra).

maria (legal): high-level checklist: 1) explicit redistribution/grant to downstream customers 2) permission to host in multi-tenant hosted environment (if applicable) 3) export control / EAR compliance statement 4) patent & trademark carveouts if needed 5) warranty / indemnity — limit claims.

cj (eng-ml): from infra side: also need clarity on model artifact format (hf repo? torchscript? safetensors?), quantized weights availability, and whether they permit us to do quantization/optimization. Some licenses ban modifications. If they forbid, we can't run optimized kernels.

samir (product): for GTM — we need to know logo usage rights, joint announcement windows, and any restrictions on co-marketing. Also revenue share or marketplace listing fees if they expect a cut when their model gets used in our Hosted or Marketplace product.

ellie (gtm): AWS/Azure marketplaces have specific distribution rules. If OpenModelX wants us to list a packaged product image for Dedicated/Private, we need an AMI/container artifact and a SaaS/marketplace contract. paging @partners-bot for the vendor marketplace intake link. :call_me_hand:

partners-bot: vendor intake form: https://rwd.partners/internal/vendor-intake — please complete the "model provider" flow and attach license + artifact manifest.

alex (partnerships): proposed next steps: 1) maria to review license and draft necessary grant language 2) cj to validate technical constraints (artifact types + allowed optimizations) 3) ellie/samir to run marketplace + announcement checklist 4) request a short SLA/support matrix from OpenModelX (how they handle CVEs, model bugs). aim to have a draft term sheet by EOD Fri. ok?

maria (legal): i'll draft a minimal clause we need. sample snippet for distribution grant (prelim):

```
Model Distribution Grant: Licensor hereby grants Redwood Inference, its affiliates, and customers a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free right to host, reproduce, distribute, modify (including quantization and optimization), sublicense, and otherwise make available the Model and Model Weights as part of Redwood's hosted services, dedicated deployments, and customer-managed private deployments, subject to export control laws and Licensor's attribution requirements.
```

maria (legal): we should also ask for a narrow indemnity for IP claims and a maximum liability cap. i'll annotate and share in a doc.

cj (eng-ml): perfect. also add an explicit permission for us to run static analysis and safety scans (to prevent downstream hallucination amplification) and to ship mitigations. e.g., prompt filters, stop-sequences.

alex (partnerships): good call. maria — can you add that to the draft?

maria (legal): yes — will add a clause: "Permission to perform security/safety analysis and to deploy mitigations". sending a redline to OpenModelX legal after internal review.

samir (product): timeline question: if they agree, can we do a soft listing in our Hosted catalog (unpublished) for internal perf testing within 2 weeks, and then a marketplace/public listing in ~6 weeks? we need 4-week lead for marketing assets + security review.

ellie (gtm): 6 weeks seems reasonable. ask OpenModelX for a point-of-contact for co-marketing, logo assets, trademark consent, and case study permission (opt-in). also confirm whether they require announcement embargo.

alex (partnerships): i'll ask them for: license text, artifact URIs, quantization allowance, support matrix, co-marketing rights, trademark/logo use, export control statement, and preferred announcement cadence. will paste replies here.

partners-bot: reminder: attach NDA/LOE to vendor intake if required.

cj (eng-ml): one more: performance profile. request sample prompts + expected latencies/QPS so we can bench on our runtime and produce cost estimates for customers.

alex (partnerships): noted — adding to the ask list.

maria (legal): small red flag: if the license contains a clause like "no commercial use" or a dual-license requiring paid license for commercial usage, we need their commercial license terms and pricing. don't onboard until commercial terms are clear.

samir (product): do we support BYOL (bring your own license) flow where customer brings model artifacts directly for Private? if so, that reduces redistribution concerns but marketplace listing still needs permissions.

cj (eng-ml): we do support BYOL for Private, but Dedicated/Hosted require redistribution grants. note that BYOL still needs us to provide runtime hooks and we must confirm patching rights.

alex (partnerships): ok — i'll push for a permissive distribution grant. if they prefer BYOL, we can offer Private-only path as fallback. i'll update once they reply. thanks all. :v:
